h1: Citrus Sukhumvit 13 Bangkok — a well-reviewed 3-star value hotel with a rooftop pool and a free tuk-tuk to BTS, from approx. THB 1,350
intro: If you want a hotel in the heart of Sukhumvit that has a rooftop pool, sits in an easy-to-reach location, and does not charge four-star rates, Citrus Sukhumvit 13 by Compass Hospitality is the name that surfaces consistently in genuine guest reviews. It is a 79-room, 3-star boutique property on Sukhumvit Soi 13 in the Nana area, with all rooms fully renovated in January 2025. Key draws are a rooftop outdoor pool with a bar above the city, and a complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle to BTS Nana, BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit — the detail that repeatedly earns it an edge over nearby competitors at a similar price. Rates start from approx. THB 1,350/night in low season, with a score of 8.7 from 984 Booking.com reviews and a Guests' Choice badge.

body.html: The straightforward reason Citrus Sukhumvit 13 accumulates more positive reviews than its budget neighbours is simple: the value proposition is unusually strong for the price. A rooftop pool, a free tuk-tuk to the nearest BTS and MRT stations, all rooms freshly overhauled in January 2025, and a front-desk team that guests name individually in their reviews — Sprite, Wan, Kamin, Lilly are all mentioned repeatedly — add up to something that feels closer to a four-star experience priced at three. The hotel is operated by Compass Hospitality, a Bangkok boutique brand with several properties in the Sukhumvit corridor.

The property sits on Sukhumvit Soi 13, neatly between BTS Nana and Asok — a position that gives easy access to both the Sukhumvit BTS Line and MRT Sukhumvit without the full noise of the main road outside the door. Room categories cover four options: Premier Room (22 sq m, king or twin) for light travellers; Premier Corner Room (28 sq m, king) with a wider window angle and slightly more breathing room; Executive Premier Room (30 sq m, king), which comes with a 55-inch Smart TV and Chromecast — an upgrade reviewers call well worth the step up; and the Family Suite with Bunk Bed (50 sq m), a separate living room plus a king bed and bunk configuration suited to families or groups of three. All rooms come with free Wi-Fi, USB charging ports, a safety deposit box, minibar, and a digital door lock.

"The rooftop pool is fantastic — the views and the atmosphere are far better than you would expect for the price. The front desk staff were incredibly friendly the whole time. We will definitely come back."

The feature that comes up most often in real guest reviews is the rooftop pool and bar. An open-air deck with sun loungers, orange umbrellas and a bar serving drinks and light food, with Sukhumvit skyline in every direction — it is genuinely difficult to find at this price point, and reviewers know it. Beyond the pool, the hotel has an in-house spa offering Thai massage and aromatherapy, useful for anyone who wants to decompress without going out. The Citrus Café handles meals and coffee on the ground floor, though the menu is lighter rather than a full dining-room affair.

On getting around: BTS Nana is approximately 650 metres away, a walk of about 8–10 minutes in Bangkok heat. The hotel's free tuk-tuk shuttle covers BTS Nana, BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit — the service that reviewers cite as the clearest practical advantage over similar properties on the same soi. From either BTS station, Terminal 21 is one stop at Asok, Siam Paragon is three stops, and Soi Cowboy plus the Nana entertainment district are within walking distance. Bumrungrad International Hospital is around 1.2 km away if that matters for your trip.

The honest part of this review: the Premier Room at 22 sq m is compact, and multiple reviews note that two people with large suitcases will feel it. Upgrading to the Premier Corner or Executive Premier is worth considering if you are staying more than a night or two. Breakfast is not included in the standard room rate — Citrus Café is there, but the surrounding streets of Soi 13 and Sukhumvit Soi 11 have a better range of options from street food to international cafés. The hotel has no gym, and a handful of reviews mention that the shower temperature control takes some getting used to. Neither point is a deal-breaker for a short city stay, but both are worth knowing.

The bottom line: Citrus Sukhumvit 13 is one of the most consistently well-reviewed affordable 3-star options in central Sukhumvit. The rooftop pool, the free shuttle, the fresh 2025 renovation and the quality of the staff make it punch above its weight for travellers who want a proper hotel experience — clean, central, friendly — without spending a premium. Rates run from around THB 1,350 in the low season to roughly THB 2,500 at peak times, which for this location and these facilities still represents genuine value.

honestSummary: Citrus Sukhumvit 13 is a 3-star hotel that reliably delivers more value than its price implies. The rooftop pool, free BTS shuttle, 2025 renovation and staff quality are real advantages, not marketing language — the review record backs them up. The trade-off is a compact entry-level room, no gym and no included breakfast. For travellers who just need a clean, well-located base in Sukhumvit and value genuine hospitality, it is hard to beat at this price.
honestChecks: If you need more space or are travelling as a couple with large bags — the 22 sq m Premier Room will feel cramped → upgrade to the Premier Corner (28 sq m) or Executive Premier (30 sq m); the price difference is modest for a meaningful comfort improvement

If you rely on included breakfast — it is not included in the standard rate → Citrus Café is available inside, or there is a wide range of street food and cafés within a short walk on the surrounding streets
If you need a gym — there is none on-site → Zenith Sukhumvit on Soi 3 nearby has a pool, gym and spa if those facilities matter to your stay

tips.title: Make full use of the free tuk-tuk
tips.body: Tell the front desk when you need a ride to BTS Nana, BTS Asok or MRT Sukhumvit — the complimentary tuk-tuk runs all day. It saves a sweaty 8-10 minute walk in Bangkok heat and beats paying for a short Grab every time.

tips.title: Rooftop pool: best in the late afternoon
tips.body: The pool deck is quietest on weekday afternoons. The Sukhumvit skyline at dusk is the nicest backdrop, and the rooftop bar is open — worth heading up after a day of sightseeing or errands before the evening crowd arrives.

tips.title: Breakfast not included — good options nearby
tips.body: No breakfast in the room rate, but Sukhumvit Soi 13 and the surrounding streets have everything from street-food stalls to international cafés open from early morning. Citrus Café inside the hotel covers basic breakfast items if you prefer to stay in.

tips.title: Getting around Bangkok from here
tips.body: Tuk-tuk to BTS Nana or Asok, then Terminal 21 is one BTS stop at Asok. Siam Paragon is three stops. For Suvarnabhumi Airport, take BTS to Phaya Thai then the Airport Rail Link — allow around 45–50 minutes total.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Citrus Sukhumvit 13 by Compass Hospitality Bangkok

faq.q: Is Citrus Sukhumvit 13 close to BTS? Does it have a shuttle?
faq.a: BTS Nana (Sukhumvit Line) is approximately 650 metres away — about an 8–10 minute walk. The hotel operates a complimentary tuk-tuk shuttle to BTS Nana, BTS Asok and MRT Sukhumvit. Just let the front desk know when you need a ride; no need to walk out in the heat or order a short Grab.

faq.q: Does Citrus Sukhumvit 13 have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor rooftop pool open to all guests, plus a rooftop bar serving drinks and light food. The pool area is one of the most-mentioned highlights in real guest reviews, consistently praised as better than expected for a hotel at this price point.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Citrus Sukhumvit 13 Bangkok?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 1,350/night for a Premier Room (22 sq m) in low season. A Premier Corner Room (28 sq m) runs around THB 1,650; the Executive Premier (30 sq m, 55-inch Smart TV) around THB 1,950; the Family Suite with Bunk Bed (50 sq m) around THB 2,800. High-season rates can reach approximately THB 2,500 for the entry-level room. Check Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com for current pricing.

faq.q: Is breakfast included at Citrus Sukhumvit 13?
faq.a: Breakfast is not included in the standard room rate. Citrus Café inside the hotel serves food and drinks throughout the day. The streets around Sukhumvit Soi 13 offer a wide range of eating options from early morning — from street-food stalls and bakeries to international cafés — within easy walking distance.

faq.q: Who is Citrus Sukhumvit 13 best suited for?
faq.a: It is best suited to travellers who want a clean, centrally located, well-staffed hotel in Sukhumvit without paying four-star rates — whether visiting for leisure, business or simply needing a reliable Bangkok base. The rooftop pool, free BTS shuttle and 2025 renovations make the value proposition unusually strong at the 3-star level. If you require a gym or included breakfast, consider stepping up to a four-star property in the same area.
